display.title: Episode 514: The Three Sacks of Gold (Rosh Chodesh Adar Rishon)
display.summary_short: On Rosh Chodesh Adar Rishon, Uncle Yossi gives reasons to increase in joy, then tells of a lazy artist who hung a mirror to claim the king's prize.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on Rosh Chodesh Adar Rishon in a leap year. Uncle Yossi explains that when Adar begins we increase our joy, and gives reasons to be happy always: every Jew has a neshamah that is truly part of Hashem, we have the Torah whose mitzvos are Hashem's will, and we pray directly to Hashem, who hears every prayer. The greatest joy will be the coming of Moshiach, and Purim reminds us of the miracles of the past. After the Hakochainik march, a young Tzivos Hashem member who knows the Twelve Pesukim by heart says the Shema, and everyone gives tzedakah. Story time: a king hires three artists to paint three walls, promising sacks of gold to the best. Two work hard for thirty days, while the third arrives on the last day with a covered mirror that reflects their paintings. The king rewards him with the 'two sacks of gold' reflected in his mirror. Uncle Yossi teaches that reward comes only from one's own effort, urges soldiers to learn the Twelve Pesukim as weapons against the yetzer hara, and gives candle-lighting times.
display.lesson: You are rewarded only for your own hard work, never for the efforts of others.

date.note: 'It's already Rosh Chodesh Adar... the first one is today' in a leap year; Tuesday 30 Shevat 5752 (1st day of Rosh Chodesh Adar I). Candle time 5:00.

sources_cited.note: Cited: we pray only to Hashem for all our needs.
